generator.params.note: Hand-set from photographs of open-grown trees: a broad, dense, rounded crown about as wide as it is tall; a short trunk that leans and divides low into three stems; opposite buds; leaves on long petioles about 0.3 m across, and leaf area per card matched to the drawn leaf. Not fitted to measurements. Growth plan G1 (2026-10-08): grown by the `sapindaceae` program (terminal flowering forks the shoots; shoots rise; space renews where limbs are shed, and limbs that no longer pay their way are shed) to 250 years (typical life 50-200 years, feis-acemac; "well over 200" in the San Juan Islands, islandhistories), with keyframes spaced roughly geometrically (and 30 years, the age ivy grows on it). Its architecture follows Scarrone's model: terminal racemes fork the shoots (Acer pseudoplatanus is Scarrone in Legner et al. 2013; see plantgen/forms/G1-ARCHITECTURE.md). Open-grown crowns are about as wide as the tree is tall and trunks 0.6-2 m dbh (feis-acemac); leaf blade 15-30 cm wide on a 15-25 cm petiole (kpu-plantdb), which the 0.4 m card with a 0.42 petiole share matches. Fitted 2026-10-08 against the Urban Tree Database (see allometry) and Joshi's photographs of open-grown trees: the crown envelope (crown_radius 8.3, crown_rate 0.027, crown_height 26, height_rate 0.038) to its crown widths and heights by age; space_density 30, space_kill 0.4 and space_reach 1.8 so shoots fill the crown finely enough that it reads as dense from the side (about 10 to 15 % see-through in plantc renders); one leaf pair a year on a short shoot (spur_pairs 1), which also keeps leaf area per crown area near the database's 6 to 7.5 m²/m²; pipe_rings 8e-6 for its dbh by age. Known gap: young crowns (30 to 70 years) hold about 50 % more leaf area than the database's trees.

allometry.note: USDA Forest Service Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005, public domain): its fitted age-to-dbh and dbh-to-height equations for bigleaf maple in the Pacific Northwest region (Longview, WA; 40 open-grown park and street trees aged 1 to 150 years), evaluated at 30, 50, 75 and 120 years. The same equations give crown diameters of 10.7, 14.4, 17.0 and 18.9 m and leaf areas of 594, 1034, 1483 and 2117 m², which the crown envelope (crown_radius, crown_rate, crown_height, height_rate) was fitted to.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs. Leaf: five deep, sparsely toothed lobes on a long petiole. Bark: shallow twisting ridges, a buttressed base and moss on the upper side of thick limbs, as on coastal trees. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: hanging racemes of paired samaras about 4 cm long, green and bristly at the seed. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) is authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: hanging racemes of yellow-green flowers in April; samaras green all summer, brown in September and October, falling into the winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth when young, then grey-brown and shallowly furrowed into narrow interlacing ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves smaller and more deeply lobed than the large thin shade leaves inside the crown; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.
